item.title: The level-one vector representation, its affinization and the energy function
item.statement: Use j=1,…,e as representatives (j=e represents0). The derived affine vector module V=⊕ Q(q)v_j has K_i v_j=q^(delta_(j≡i)−delta_(j≡i+1))v_j, E_i v_j=delta_(j≡i+1)v_(j−1), F_i v_j=delta_(j≡i)v_(j+1), indices cyclic. Its P_cl weight is Lambda_j−Lambda_(j−1), level0; its finite crystal has f_i b_i=b_(i+1), e_i b_(i+1)=b_i, epsilon(b_j)=Lambda_(j−1)^cl and phi(b_j)=Lambda_j^cl, level1. The full affinization has u_(j−ae)=z^a v_j of P-weight Lambda_j−Lambda_(j−1)+a delta and K_d eigen q^a. Equivalently E_i(z^a v_j)=delta_(j≡i+1) z^(a+delta_(i,0))v_(j−1), F_i(z^a v_j)=delta_(j≡i) z^(a−delta_(i,0))v_(j+1). Thus E_i u_m=delta_(m≡i+1)u_(m−1), F_i u_m=delta_(m≡i)u_(m+1). Ordinary order is u_m>u_n iff m>n. The energy is explicitly in the OPPOSITE tensor-crystal channel of KMPY bar-Delta-plus (opposite our fixed Delta): H_op(z^a b_j⊗z^b b_k)=chi(j>k)+b−a, and l(z^a b_j)=ae−j. It has the two loop-shift axioms, is constant on that channel's components, is0 on extremal diagonals and H_op>0 iff m1>m2. For a fixed charge M the ground sequence is b°_s=u_(M−s), s≥0: epsilon(b°_s)=phi(b°_(s+1)) and H_op(b°_s,b°_(s+1))=1. It is determined after the initial phase/loop vector (hence charge) is fixed, not independently of an overall loop shift. All statements include e=2.
item.strategy: Check E/F/K on the explicit u_m: each color acts on disjoint pairs (u_(i+ke),u_(i+ke+1)), with K eigen q,q^-1 and zero second powers. Different-color mixed commutators and the cycle Serre sums follow directly from these shifts; the e=2 cubic sums vanish because each squared single-color operator is0. The z-shifts on the0 edge give [d,E0]=E0,[d,F0]=−F0 and the displayed P-weights; forgetting d leaves only P_cl, not a full P-grading on finite V. Compute epsilon/phi from the arrows. KMPY uses b_j^src→b_(j+1) here and its ground indexk→u_(1−k); its MAIN bar-Delta-plus and tensor rule(2.2.13) were visually read. In that OP channel inspect the two-index rule: non-wrap moves do not change chi except at the coincident/adjacent case where the rule selects the other factor, and wrap moves change chi by the opposite of the loop-power change. This proves H_op constancy including the ties/e=2. For m1=j−ae,m2=k−be, the cases b−a positive/zero/negative prove H_op>0 iff m1>m2. The ground identities are the wrap/nonwrap calculation with adjacent integer indices. The bridge lemma later constructs the actual normalized R; no field R property is imported from the unavailable KMN source.

(iii) The flipped operator $R_{\mathrm{op}}:=PR_{\mathrm{fix}}P$ with
$\psi_{\mathrm{op}}=1-q^2a$ is the opposite-channel ($\otimes_+$) normalized
braiding of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]:
its $q^0$-leading term is
$z^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}b_1\otimes z^{-H_{\mathrm{op}}}b_2$ with the energy
$H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k)=\chi(j>k)+b-a$, and its kernel is
$N_{\mathrm{op}}=P\ker(S+1)$, the $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-orbit of the extremal
diagonal generated by
$C_{j,k}=v_j\otimes z^{-\chi(j>k)}v_k+q\,z^{-\chi(j>k)}v_k\otimes v_j$ $(j\ne k)$
and $C_{j,j}=v_j\otimes v_j$. Flipping back gives the fixed-channel quotient
and the normal-ordering relations of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]].

[F3] On residue pairs $(j,k)$ the opposite-channel rule is $f$ on the first factor iff $\varepsilon_i(b_1)\ge\varphi_i(b_2)$, and $H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k)=\chi(j>k)+b-a$ satisfies the two loop-shift axioms and $H_{\mathrm{op}}>0\iff m_1>m_2$ ([[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]).
